Building on Calinou's comment, we used to have a roughness_fade term that would make SSR fade away as we approached 0.6 roughness. If we want to keep this cutoff we should restore a bit of a fade to ease the transition between SSR and whatever we are falling back to.

In the long term, the different indirect specular methods need to be more aware of each other. But a simple fade would be fine for now

I've made it apply a smooth fade from 0.5 roughness to 0.6 to smoothen out the transitions.
@Calinou Could you check how it looks in your test scene now?

Looks better to me, although I wonder if we should increase the roughness cutoff to `0.65` and start the fade at `0.55` to compensate for the smooth fade making SSR less noticeable.

In the long run, we should check what other engines use as a value for their roughness cutoff, but I recall it being higher than `0.65`; probably between `0.7` and `0.8`.

body: Needs a description

These are the old NTSC/PAL luminance weights. They should probably be the Rec. 709 luminance weights. I recommend labelling them as such so that they will be easy to adapt to other colour primaries in the future (godotengine/godot-proposals#12783):

```suggestion
	const vec3 rec709_luminance_weights = vec3(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722);
	color.rgb /= 1.0 - dot(color.rgb, rec709_luminance_weights); // Invert the tone mapping we applied in the main trace pass.
```
Are negative lights possible? FYI, I took this tonemapping idea from the glow shader.
I went and increased the roughness cutoff to 0.7 since there's plenty budget for it with the new code.

> Are negative lights possible? FYI, I took this tonemapping idea from the glow shader.

Yes, for better or for worse, negative lights are fully supported in Godot. A strong negative light should always clip to black before being presented to the screen; this happens implicitly when writing to the final swapchain buffer or explicitly before appying tonemappers that would behave poorly with negative values in `tonemap.glsl` or `post.glsl`.

I haven't tested this myself, but my expectation from glancing at this code is that strong negative lights that result in a colour value of `-1.01` for example would produce a large positive value to to this tonemapping function's asymptote at `-1.0`. For this reason, colour values likely would need to be clipped to zero before performing this function.

But again, I haven't tested it; this is conjecture on my part, but something worth looking into if you haven't already.

(Also, I can't see this sort of tonemapping applying in the glow shader, unless you're talking about how softlight is blended in `tonemap.glsl`?)
Here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/copy.glsl#L107

> Here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/copy.glsl#L107

Ah, thanks! These are actually on my list of luminance weights to update when I have the time.

I believe it's entirely possible the same issue that I'm describing could happen with glow; negative lights are rarely tested, so the bug could have gone unnoticed for a long time. Both this PR and the existing glow might need to be fixed if my theoretical problem can be reproduced...

(For testing negative lights, make sure to have HDR 2D enabled and use the Compatibility or Forward+ rendering method.)

Continuing the discussion from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111210#discussion_r2445177856, this needs testing with negative lights in Forward+ with  HDR 2D enabled to ensure that `color` values around `-1.01` and smaller don't behave poorly. If they do, then `color` will likely need to be clipped to be non-negative after it is read via `textureLod`.
We should just clip to 0.0 when copying from the last frame texture. I don't think there is any reason to try to handle negative colours here.

Actually, we might already clip to positive values already. I remember adding code to filter out NaNs and INFs when copying the texture for SSIL. I think I clipped to a reasonable range as well

_edit: Nevermind, it only filters out NaN and INF, we should clip out negatives too_
